screens.title: Fashion Matters
screens.instruction: Look at the fashion image. In pairs, discuss what clothes can communicate about a person. Choose one idea and explain your opinion.
screens.question: What matters most when you choose clothes?

screens.title: Talk about fashion
screens.instruction: Work with a partner. Discuss the questions below. First think quietly for 20 seconds, then take turns answering and asking one follow-up question.
questions: How important is fashion to you?
What sort of clothes do you prefer to wear?
Do you ever have to wear things you don’t really like? If so, when and why?

screens.title: Four ways to expand an answer
screens.instruction: Watch the video and identify the four ways to expand an answer. Then explore the technique cards one by one and use the useful phrases to improve your own answers.

items.title: Give a reason
items.support: Because… / The main reason is that…
items.model: I prefer comfortable clothes because I move around a lot during the day.

items.title: Give an example
items.model: For example, I usually wear trainers when I go to university.

items.title: Add a contrast
items.support: However… / Unlike… / In the past…, but now…
items.model: I used to follow trends, but now I care more about comfort.

items.title: Give an opinion
items.model: Personally, I think clothes can show part of your personality.

screens.title: Build your fashion vocabulary
screens.instruction: Choose one category at a time. Read the words aloud, then add one more example of your own.

screens.title: Describe and compare the people
screens.instruction: Work in pairs. Choose one pair of photos. First describe what each person is wearing and their appearance. Then make one comparison. Your partner should add one extra detail.
screens.note: Comparison language is preview/support only. Systematic comparison work belongs to U1.2.

screens.title: Who is speaking?
screens.instruction: Listen to Speakers 2–5 and match each speaker to the correct photo. Compare your answers with a partner, then check the speakers one by one.

screens.title: Find the phrasal verbs
screens.instruction: Select Speakers 2–5 in turn. Read each transcript, identify the phrasal verbs, and try to explain their meaning from context before checking.

items.meaning: understand or follow something that is changing fast
be easy to see or notice
keep money for something in the future

screens.title: How do phrasal verbs work?
screens.instruction: Watch the video. Discuss the three questions below with a partner. Click each question only after you have agreed on an answer.

items.question: What is a phrasal verb?
items.answer: A phrasal verb is a verb together with an adverb or preposition that changes its meaning.

items.question: What two types can you identify?
items.answer: Two-part: verb + adverb/preposition. Three-part: verb + adverb + preposition.

items.question: What do you notice about word order?
items.answer: Some two-part phrasal verbs can be separated; three-part phrasal verbs are not separated in the patterns taught here.

screens.title: Listen, identify, then match
screens.instruction: Step 1: Listen again to Speakers 2–5 and identify the phrasal verbs you hear. The list includes distractors. Step 2: Match the nine target phrasal verbs to their definitions.

matching.definition: understand something that is changing fast
create something by joining or combining different things
keep money for something in the future
be easy to see or notice

screens.title: Phrasal verbs with go
screens.instruction: Complete each sentence with the correct form of go and a particle from the box. Explain the meaning of your choice, then reveal each answer separately.

items.text: The prices of leather bags have ___ a lot recently.
Why are you looking at me like that? What’s ___?
The design company ___ the applicant with the best portfolio.
I ___ to the same shoe shop but there were no more pairs in my size.
You’ll need to ___ all the figures in the report to check they’re correct.

screens.title: Complete Emma’s letter
screens.instruction: Complete the letter with phrasal verbs from Exercise 7. More than one answer may be possible. Compare your choices, then reveal each blank separately.

screens.title: What advice would you give Emma?
screens.instruction: Work in pairs. Give Emma two or three pieces of advice. For each piece of advice, give a reason or an example. Try to use at least two phrasal verbs from the lesson.

screens.title: Can you remember it?
screens.instruction: Answer each challenge aloud before revealing the sample answer. Check one card at a time.

items.prompt: Name 3 words for clothing or appearance.
Give 2 phrasal verbs from the listening.
Which phrasal verb means “be easy to notice”?
Give Emma one piece of advice.
items.answer: You could wear what makes you feel confident.

screens.title: Before you leave…
screens.instruction: Take one minute. Write or say one new phrasal verb you learned, one thing you can now do better, and one point you still want to practise.

screens.title: Reply to Emma
screens.label: Teacher-added Extension
screens.instruction: Write a short reply to Emma. Give clear advice, explain your reasons, and use three or four phrasal verbs from the lesson naturally and accurately.

screens.title: Thank You
screens.instruction: You have completed Unit 1.1 – Fashion Matters.
